headline: Two of every three park fountains tested in Ward 12 came back flagged for lead.
summary:
Three in four households in Ward 12 speak something other than English at home, the third-highest share in Chicago. That's one piece of a ward sitting at 31st of 50 overall, in the lower half of the city. Ward 12 covers Brighton Park, McKinley Park, New City, and the Lower West Side on the Southwest Side. The ward also carries one of the lowest shares of people living alone in Chicago, and it ranks second on participatory budgeting, meaning residents get a direct vote on how the ward's menu money gets spent.

The weaker numbers touch health access and everyday gathering spots. Ward 12 has the second-lowest count of mental health providers per resident in Chicago, and sits behind most of Chicago on third places, the cafes, bars, restaurants, and gyms where people spend informal time. Recorded real estate sales run low too, and the ward used only about 70 percent of its yearly aldermanic menu budget in the most recent full year, one of the lower utilization rates in Chicago. The starkest number sits at the park level, where Ward 12 sits in last place, 50th of 50, on the share of park fountains carrying a historically elevated lead reading.
reading_the_rankings: A couple of these figures deserve a closer look. Ward 12's second-place score on participatory budgeting looks close to the top, but the field crowding that score runs thirteen wards deep before it drops two points, so second and several wards below it aren't meaningfully far apart. The 49th-place mark on mental health providers, 0.9 per 10,000 residents, looks close to the worst in Chicago, but the crowd stuck near that same low score runs twenty-two wards deep before it climbs two points. The middle fifty percent of wards on this measure crowd into a narrow seven-point band too, so a lot of the city sits close to that same low mark, and Ward 12's rank comes from landing inside that band. The park fountain lead figure carries none of that hedging. Two out of three of the ward's tested fountains came back flagged, and the source attaches no caveat to that number.

news.headline: New Housing OK'd For Avondale, McKinley Park, Streeterville And Across From Johnny's Icehouse
news.note: The City Council's zoning committee approved a 199-apartment, nine-townhome development at 3033 S. Justine St. in McKinley Park, in Ald. Julia Ramirez's ward.

news.headline: Riverfront Data Center In McKinley Park Revives Expansion Plans But Faces Delay
news.note: QTS Data Center's plan to expand its McKinley Park riverfront campus hit a permitting delay, and Ald. Julia Ramirez said any expansion should show public benefits matched to its infrastructure demands.

news.headline: 'Moving Archer Forward' Initiative Aims To Bring 800 New Housing Units To Archer Avenue
news.note: The same Archer Avenue plan, about 800 housing units and 280,000 square feet of retail along a 6.3-mile stretch, runs through Brighton Park and McKinley Park on its way from Bridgeport to Garfield Ridge.
